candidates.source_name: NBS – Register podľa PSD2 (machine-readable payment institution register)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative regulator register of every SK-licensed payment institution, e-money institution, AISP/PISP/PIISP — the definitive population frame for the SK PSP/acquirer competitor set, with a documented JSON API (subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2) and a signed variant, updated daily.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled JSON pull of https://subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2 (daily/weekly), diff on entity list to detect new entrants, licence extensions and exits
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search for regulator register terms
queries_used: NBS zoznam platobných inštitúcií register poskytovateľov platobných služieb Slovensko

candidates.source_name: NBS – Payment institutions and AISP supervision pages
candidates.why_relevant: Supervisory narrative layer around the register: licensing conditions, categories of authorisation, notifications of passporting — explains what each competitor is actually permitted to do in SK.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML fetch + change detection on the supervision section
queries_used: NBS zoznam platobných inštitúcií register poskytovateľov platobných služieb Slovensko

candidates.source_name: NBS – Zoznam účastníkov platobného systému SIPS
candidates.why_relevant: Participant list for the domestic SIPS clearing system — reveals which banks/PSPs have direct clearing access in SK versus those riding on a sponsor, a key structural fact about the payments landscape.

candidates.source_name: NBS – SEPA Instant Credit Transfer / payment instruments & payment cards statistics

candidates.why_relevant: SBA publishes monthly SK card issuing AND acquiring statistics (cards, ATM and POS terminal transactions) and owns the PAY by square QR standard incl. its terms-of-use/specification PDF; SBA is also the SK NASO for EPC SEPA scheme adherence.

negative_findings.description: No SK-specific Nexi presence (acquiring entity, SK-localised site, or SK terminal offer) surfaced despite a targeted bilingual query pairing Nexi with Slovak terminal/acquiring vocabulary; results returned only Worldline SK pages and generic Nexi Southern-Europe descriptions.
negative_findings.result_summary: Nexi appears in pan-European provider write-ups but no sk-SK domain, SK press release or SK licence trace was found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If Nexi has no direct SK footprint, the SK acquiring competitor set is materially narrower (Global Payments, Worldline, bank arms, domestic PSPs) and any market map that lists Nexi as an SK acquirer is wrong.

negative_findings.description: No Slovak terminal-hardware distributor or vendor-partner page for Ingenico, PAX or Verifone was found; the local-language query returned only US/NL resellers.
negative_findings.result_summary: SK-side hardware channel for terminal OEMs is not visible through generic search with terms 'distribútor', 'dodávateľ', 'platobné terminály'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Terminal OEM/estate share in SK is a core question for this cell; without a distributor layer it must be inferred from acquirer product pages (Worldline Yomani/Yoximo/Valina/Axium; Global Payments terminal line-up) or from public procurement and tender records.

negative_findings.description: Targeted search for SK merchant case studies / references published by TrustPay, Besteron, ComGate, GoPay and Barion returned comparison articles rather than any case-study or reference page.
negative_findings.result_summary: No PSP-published SK case study located via search; these usually live on vendor sites behind non-indexed paths.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Case studies are the primary evidence of which merchants and verticals each PSP actually holds; they must be harvested by crawling each vendor site directly rather than via search engines.

negative_findings.description: TrustPay's canonical corporate domain was not returned by any search result in this pass; trustpay.eu is an inference from the entity's well-known naming and is recorded with low confidence.
negative_findings.result_summary: Entity confirmed (SK-founded 2009, NBS payment-institution licence) but URL unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A wrong canonical domain would silently break monitoring for a top-tier domestic PSP; resolve via the NBS PSD2 register entity record before adding to collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-owned acquiring arms and their gateway brands (Tatra banka CardPay, VÚB eCard, ČSOB, 365.bank, Slovenská sporiteľňa) were only reached indirectly via comparison articles and one bank partner page; their own acceptance/pricing pages were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the business/merchant-acceptance section of each major SK bank site (terminál, platobná brána, prijímanie kariet) and register each as a direct source with quarterly snapshots.

coverage_gaps.description: No public-procurement or tender source was scouted, although SK state and municipal bodies procure POS terminals, acquiring and payment gateways — a category that names vendors, volumes and prices explicitly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the SK public-procurement portal (ÚVO/EVO) and the central contracts register (CRZ) with keyword monitors for 'platobný terminál', 'akceptácia platobných kariet', 'platobná brána'.

coverage_gaps.description: A2A/instant-payments commercial actors beyond the scheme registers — VOP, Request-to-Pay, and open-banking PISP-based checkout in SK — were only touched via SKPAY and generic EPC material; Viamo was named but no primary source was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Filter the NBS PSD2 JSON for PISP/AISP authorisations to build the SK open-banking actor list, then scout each entity's own site; specifically resolve Viamo's operating entity and domain.

coverage_gaps.description: Card-scheme SK activity is currently sourced only through re-published PR; no Visa or Mastercard SK-market page, local interchange/fee disclosure, or SK licensee list was scouted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout Visa and Mastercard SK/CEE market pages, their published EEA interchange and scheme-fee disclosures, and any SK licensed-acquirer listings the schemes publish.

coverage_gaps.description: All URLs in this slice are search-derived and none were fetched; several (NBS deep links, EPC register paths, worldline sk-SK deep paths) are long and prone to redirect or restructure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the deterministic liveness pass and, on non-200, retry the section root rather than marking the source dead.

brief: The SK payments landscape has an unusually strong regulatory spine: NBS's PSD2 register (with a daily-updated JSON API and a signed variant), the SIPS participant list and NBS payment statistics together give a machine-readable, authoritative frame of every licensed SK PSP, e-money institution and clearing participant, complemented by the Slovak Banking Association's monthly card issuing/acquiring statistics and its ownership of the PAY by square QR standard. The commercial layer splits into international acquirers with SK-localised estates (Global Payments s.r.o., distributed partly through Slovenská sporiteľňa; Worldline with sk-SK merchant terminal and FI acquiring/ATM lines), domestic licensed PSPs (Besteron/Seyfor, TrustPay, 24-pay, SKPAY) and CZ/HU entrants (ComGate, GoPay, Barion), with bank-owned gateway brands (CardPay, eCard) forming a distinct fourth layer that is currently visible mainly through third-party comparisons. Indirect and financial sources are strong — registeruz.sk and FinStat expose local revenue for each SK-registered payments entity, and e-commerce platform integration lists plus SAEC/MNFORCE payment-method studies reveal the gateway estate from the merchant side. The main gaps are terminal-OEM channel visibility (no SK Ingenico/PAX/Verifone distributor surfaced), the absence of any public-procurement source, unconfirmed Nexi presence in SK, and vendor case studies that will need direct site crawling rather than search.
